homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name: the capture's reached kind is 'same'. 'ELMCIP' names both the project (2010–2013) and the knowledge base; the census's aka gives 'ELMCIP Knowledge Base', 'Electronic Literature Knowledge Base' and 'ELMCIP' as names of the knowledge base, and card 2 is a second domain under the name (www.elmcip.it), the project's site. The distinct entities below are named by the field, the census or the archive beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the ELMCIP project, Electronic Literature as a Model of Creativity and Innovation in Practice (HERA, 2010–2013), the research project of which the knowledge base is an outcome (B1 F6; B2 F21; B3 F38)
the Digital Narrative Knowledge Base, the stated successor (B1 F7; TLL-30), an entity of its own
the University of Bergen Electronic Literature Research Group (BEL), the developer (B1 F6; B3), an organization
Scott Rettberg, the project director and the essay's author (B3 F37), a person
CELL, the Consortium on Electronic Literature, which lists the knowledge base among its member archives (TLL-34; B3 F67, F70), its own census row
the Electronic Literature Collection, whose volumes it records (B1 F18; TLL-35), its own census row
the ELMCIP Anthology of European Electronic Literature (B2 F31), a publication of the project
the Electronic Literature Directory and NT2, other databases of the field (B3), distinct resources
the Electronic Literature Foundation, named in the archive (#301) among digital poetics, an organization distinct from the knowledge base

captures.description: THE KNOWLEDGE BASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The ELMCIP Electronic Literature Knowledge Base is a comprehensive, cross-referenced digital humanities research resource for electronic literature, preserved as a frozen archive on the ELMCIP Official Website.' Key details: status ('Frozen archive (active from June 2010 to October 2026; no longer open for new submissions or contributions)'); origin (Drupal 7, the University of Bergen group, 'the six-nation ELMCIP project (Electronic Literature as a Model of Creativity and Innovation in Practice, 2010–2013) led by Scott Rettberg'); content ('thousands of interconnected records'); legacy (the Digital Narrative Knowledge Base); a follow-up offer. Five cards: the ELMCIP Knowledge Base, www.elmcip.it, electronic book review, Arquivo Digital da PO.EX, a Facebook post of the Knowledge Base.

atoms.evidence: The ELMCIP Electronic Literature Knowledge Base is a comprehensive, cross-referenced digital humanities research resource for electronic literature
by the University of Bergen Electronic Literature Research Group
no longer open for new submissions or contributions
Houses thousands of interconnected records covering authors, creative works, critical writing, platforms, events, organizations, publishers, and teaching resources.
comprehensive, cross-referenced digital humanities research resource for electronic literature
Its mission continues through the transition toward the Digital Narrative Knowledge Base.
